paras.label: A
sents: Rooftops covered with grass, vegetable gardens and lush foliage are now a common sight in many cities around the world.
More and more private companies and city authorities are investing in green roofs, drawn to their wide-ranging benefits.
Among the benefits are saving on energy costs, mitigating the risk of floods, making habitats for urban wildlife, tackling air pollution and even growing food.
These increasingly radical urban designs can help cities adapt to the monumental problems they face, such as access to resources and a lack of green space due to development.

But the involvement of city authorities, businesses and other institutions is crucial to ensuring their success – as is research investigating different options to suit the variety of rooftop spaces found in cities.
The UK is relatively new to developing green roofs, and local governments and institutions are playing a major role in spreading the practice.

London is home to much of the UK's green roof market, mainly due to forward-thinking policies such as the London Plan, which has paved the way to more than doubling the area of green roofs in the capital.

simp.text: Green roofs are now a common sight.
Companies and authorities are investing in them.
Benefits: energy costs, floods, wildlife, air pollution, food
They help cities adapt to problems.
But involvement of authorities is crucial.
The UK is new; governments play a major role.
London has much of the market thanks to policies.

paras.main: Mái xanh có nhiều lợi ích và đang lan rộng nhờ chính quyền.

paras.label: B
sents: Ongoing research is showcasing how green roofs in cities can integrate with 'living walls': environmentally friendly walls which are partially or completely covered with greenery, including a growing medium, such as soil or water.

Research also indicates that green roofs can be integrated with drainage systems on the ground, such as street trees, so that the water is managed better and the built environment is made more sustainable.
There is also evidence to demonstrate the social value of green roofs.
Doctors are increasingly prescribing time spent gardening outdoors for patients dealing with anxiety and depression.
And research has found that access to even the most basic green spaces can provide a better quality of life for dementia sufferers and help people avoid obesity.

simp.text: Green roofs can integrate with living walls
They can integrate with drainage systems such as street trees
There is evidence of social value.
Doctors prescribe gardening for anxiety and depression
Green spaces help people avoid obesity

paras.main: Mái xanh kết hợp với các sáng kiến khác và có giá trị xã hội.

paras.label: C
sents: In North America, green roofs have become mainstream, with a wide array of expansive, accessible and food-producing roofs installed in buildings.
Again, city leaders and authorities have helped push the movement forward – only recently, San Francisco, USA, created a policy requiring new buildings to have green roofs.
Toronto, Canada, has policies dating from the 1990s, encouraging the development of urban farms on rooftops.
These countries also benefit from having newer buildings than in many parts of the world, which makes it easier to install green roofs.

Being able to keep enough water at roof height and distribute it right across the rooftop is crucial to maintaining the plants on any green roof – especially on 'edible roofs' where fruit and vegetables are farmed.
And it's much easier to do this in newer buildings, which can typically hold greater weight, than to retro-fit old ones.
Having a stronger roof also makes it easier to grow a greater variety of plants, since the soil can be deeper.

simp.text: Green roofs have become mainstream in North America.
City leaders pushed forward; San Francisco recently created a policy.
Toronto has policies from the 1990s
These countries have newer buildings.
Keeping and distributing enough water is crucial.
Newer buildings can hold greater weight
A stronger roof allows a greater variety of plants

paras.main: Ở Bắc Mỹ mái xanh phổ biến, và nhà mới giúp lắp mái dễ hơn.

paras.label: D
sents: For green roofs to become the norm for new developments, there needs to be support from public authorities and private investors.
Those responsible for maintaining buildings may have to acquire new skills, such as landscaping, and in some cases, volunteers may be needed to help out.

Other considerations include installing drainage paths, meeting health and safety requirements and perhaps allowing access for the public, as well as planning restrictions and disruption from regular activities in and around the buildings during installation.
To convince investors and developers that installing green roofs is worthwhile, economic arguments are still the most important.

The term 'natural capital' has been developed to explain the economic value of nature; for example, measuring the money saved by installing natural solutions to protect against flood damage, adapt to climate change or help people lead healthier and happier lives.

simp.text: Green roofs need support from authorities and investors.
Many considerations: skills, volunteers, drainage, safety, restrictions, disruption
To convince investors, economic arguments are the most important
'Natural capital' explains the economic value of nature.

paras.main: Để mái xanh thành chuẩn, cần hỗ trợ và lập luận kinh tế.

paras.label: E
sents: As the expertise about green roofs grows, official standards have been developed to ensure that they are designed, constructed and maintained properly, and function well.
Improvements in the science and technology underpinning green roof development have also led to new variations in the concept.
For example, 'blue roofs' enable buildings to hold water over longer periods of time, rather than draining it away quickly - crucial in times of heavier rainfall.
There are also combinations of green roofs with solar panels, and 'brown roofs' which are wilder in nature and maximise biodiversity.
If the trend continues, it could create new jobs and a more vibrant and sustainable local food economy - alongside many other benefits.
There are still barriers to overcome, but the evidence so far indicates that green roofs have the potential to transform cities and help them function sustainably long into the future.
The success stories need to be studied and replicated elsewhere, to make green, blue, brown and food-producing roofs the norm in cities around the world.

Improvements have led to new variations.
Blue roofs hold water longer.
Combinations with solar panels
brown roofs maximise biodiversity
The trend could create jobs.
There are still barriers, but green roofs can transform cities.
Success stories need to be studied and replicated

sents: Over the past century, a powerful idea has taken root in the educational landscape.

The concept of intelligence as something innate has been supplanted by the idea that intelligence is not fixed, and that, with the right training, we can be the authors of our own cognitive capabilities.
Psychologist Alfred Binet, the developer of the first intelligence tests, was one of many 19th-century scientists who held that earlier view and sought to quantify cognitive ability.
Then, in the early 20th century, progressive thinkers revolted against the notion that inherent ability is destiny.
Instead, educators such as John Dewey argued that every child's intelligence could be developed, given the right environment.

simp.text: A powerful idea has taken root.
Innate intelligence has been supplanted by the idea that intelligence is not fixed.
Binet held that earlier view
Then, in the early 20th century, thinkers revolted
Dewey argued intelligence could be developed.

paras.main: Quan niệm trí thông minh cố định dần bị thay bằng quan niệm có thể phát triển.

sents: 'Growth mindset theory' is a relatively new – and extremely popular – version of this idea.
In many schools today you will see hallways covered in motivational posters and hear speeches on the mindset of great sporting heroes who simply believed their way to the top.
A major focus of the growth mindset in schools is coaxing students away from seeing failure as an indication of their ability, and towards seeing it as a chance to improve that ability.
As educationalist Jeff Howard noted several decades ago: 'Smart is not something that you just are, smart is something that you can get.'

simp.text: Growth mindset theory is a new, popular version.
Schools use motivational posters and speeches.
The focus is seeing failure as a chance to improve ability
'Smart is something you can get.'

paras.main: Trường học khuyến khích học sinh tin vào khả năng cải thiện.

sents: The idea of the growth mindset is based on the work of psychologist Carol Dweck in California in the 1990s.
In one key experiment, Dweck divided a group of 10- to 12-year-olds into two groups.
All were told that they had achieved a high score on a test but the first group were praised for their intelligence in achieving this, while the others were praised for their effort.
The second group – those who had been instilled with a 'growth mindset' – were subsequently far more likely to put effort into future tasks.
Meanwhile, the former took on only those tasks that would not risk their sense of worth.
This group had inferred that success or failure is due to innate ability, and this 'fixed mindset' had led them to fear of failure and lack of effort.
Praising ability actually made the students perform worse, while praising effort emphasised that change was possible.

simp.text: Based on Dweck's work.
Two groups: praised for intelligence vs effort.
The effort group put in more effort later.
The intelligence group took only safe tasks
They feared failure
Praising ability made students perform worse.

paras.main: Khen nỗ lực tốt hơn khen năng lực.

sents: One of the greatest impediments to successfully implementing a growth mindset, however, is the education system itself: in many parts of the world, the school climate is obsessed with performance in the form of constant testing, analysing and ranking of students – a key characteristic of the fixed mindset.
Nor is it unusual for schools to create a certain cognitive dissonance, when they applaud the benefits of a growth mindset but then hand out fixed target grades in lessons based on performance.

simp.text: However, one of the greatest impediments is the education system itself.
Schools applaud growth mindset but hand out fixed target grades.

paras.main: Hệ thống giáo dục cản trở việc áp dụng growth mindset.

sents: Aside from the implementation problem, the original growth mindset research has also received harsh criticism.
The statistician Andrew Gelman claims that 'their research designs have enough degrees of freedom that they could take their data to support just about any theory at all'.
Professor of Psychology Timothy Bates, who has been trying to replicate Dweck's work, is finding that the results are repeatedly null.
He notes that: 'People with a growth mindset don't cope any better with failure ... Kids with the growth mindset aren't getting better grades, either before or after our intervention study.'

simp.text: The original research has received harsh criticism.
Gelman: research designs have too much freedom
Bates: results are repeatedly null
Kids are not getting better grades

paras.main: Nghiên cứu gốc bị phê bình về phương pháp và không tái lập được.

sents: Much of this criticism is not lost on Dweck, and she deserves great credit for responding to it and adapting her work accordingly.
In fact, she argues that her work has been misunderstood and misapplied in a range of ways.

She has also expressed concerns that her theories are being misappropriated in schools by being conflated with the self-esteem movement: 'For me the growth mindset is a tool for learning and improvement.
It's not just a vehicle for making children feel good.'

simp.text: Dweck deserves credit for responding and adapting
She argues her work has been misunderstood and misapplied
She is concerned it is conflated with the self-esteem movement.
It's not just for making children feel good

paras.main: Dweck phản hồi phê bình và nói thuyết của bà bị hiểu sai.

sents: But there is another factor at work here.
The failure to translate the growth mindset into the classroom might reflect a misunderstanding of the nature of teaching and learning itself.
Growth mindset supporters David Yeager and Gregory Walton claim that interventions should be delivered in a subtle way to maximise their effectiveness.
They say that if adolescents perceive a teacher's intervention as conveying that they are in need of help, this could undo its intended effects.

simp.text: But there is another factor.
The failure might reflect a misunderstanding of teaching and learning.
Yeager and Walton: interventions should be subtle
If students perceive the intervention as help, it could undo its effects.

paras.main: Can thiệp nên tinh tế, nếu không sẽ phản tác dụng.

sents: A lot of what drives students is their innate beliefs and how they perceive themselves.
There is a strong correlation between self-perception and achievement, but there is evidence to suggest that the actual effect of achievement on self-perception is stronger than the other way round.
To stand up in a classroom and successfully deliver a good speech is a genuine achievement, and that is likely to be more powerfully motivating than vague notions of 'motivation' itself.

simp.text: Students are driven by beliefs and self-perception.
There is a strong correlation, but the effect of achievement on self-perception is stronger
A genuine achievement is more motivating than vague notions.

paras.main: Thành tích thật sự thúc đẩy học sinh hơn là lời động viên chung chung.

sents: Recent evidence would suggest that growth mindset interventions are not the elixir of student learning that its proponents claim it to be.
The growth mindset appears to be a viable construct in the lab, which, when administered in the classroom via targeted interventions, doesn't seem to work.
It is hard to dispute that having faith in the capacity to change is a good attribute for students.
Paradoxically, however, that aspiration is not well served by direct interventions that try to instil it.

simp.text: Recent evidence suggests interventions are not an elixir.
It works in the lab but not in the classroom.
It is hard to dispute that faith in change is a good attribute.
However, direct interventions do not serve it well

paras.main: Can thiệp trực tiếp không hiệu quả dù niềm tin vào thay đổi là tốt.

sents: Motivational posters and talks are often a waste of time, and might well give students a deluded notion of what success actually means.

Teaching concrete skills such as how to write an effective introduction to an essay then praising students' effort in getting there is probably a far better way of improving confidence than telling them how unique they are, or indeed how capable they are of changing their own brains.
Perhaps growth mindset works best as a philosophy and not an intervention.

simp.text: Posters and talks are often a waste of time and might give a deluded notion
Teaching concrete skills then praising effort is better.
Perhaps it works best as a philosophy, not an intervention.

groups.instr: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 2?

items.q: Dweck has handled criticisms of her work in an admirable way.
items.exp: Đoạn 6 ①: `she deserves great credit for responding to it and adapting her work`. `handled criticisms ... in an admirable way`.

items.q: Students' self-perception is a more effective driver of self-confidence than actual achievement is.
items.exp: Đoạn 8 ②: tác động của thành tích lên tự nhận thức mạnh hơn chiều ngược lại. Đề đảo chiều: "self-perception ... more effective ... than achievement" → mâu thuẫn.

items.q: Recent evidence about growth mindset interventions has attracted unfair coverage in the media.
items.exp: Không có đoạn nào nói giới truyền thông đưa tin thiếu công bằng về bằng chứng gần đây (đoạn 9 chỉ nói bằng chứng gần đây cho thấy can thiệp không hiệu quả).

items.q: Deliberate attempts to encourage students to strive for high achievement may have a negative effect.
items.exp: Đoạn 9 ③ (`aspiration is not well served by direct interventions`) và đoạn 10 ① (`motivational posters ... might well give students a deluded notion`). `deliberate attempts ... may have a negative effect`.

sents: This is a book about the life and scientific work of Alfred Wegener, whose reputation today rests with his theory of continental displacements, better known as 'continental drift'.
Wegener proposed this theory in 1912 and developed it extensively for nearly 20 years.
His book on the subject, The Origin of Continents and Oceans, went through four editions and was the focus of an international controversy in his lifetime and for some years after his death.

simp.text: This is a book about Wegener, whose reputation rests with continental drift.
He proposed it in 1912.
His book was the focus of an international controversy in his lifetime

paras.main: Thuyết trôi dạt lục địa của Wegener gây tranh cãi quốc tế.

sents: Wegener's basic idea was that many mysteries about the Earth's history could be solved if one supposed that the continents moved laterally, rather than supposing that they remained fixed in place.

Wegener showed in great detail how such continental movements were plausible and how they worked, using evidence from a large number of sciences including geology, geophysics, paleontology, and climatology.
Wegener's idea – that the continents move – is at the heart of the theory that guides Earth sciences today: namely plate tectonics.

Plate tectonics is in many respects quite different from Wegener's proposal, in the same way that modern evolutionary theory is very different from the ideas Charles Darwin proposed in the 1850s about biological evolution.
Yet plate tectonics is a descendant of Alfred Wegener's theory of continental drift, in quite the same way that modern evolutionary theory is a descendant of Darwin's theory of natural selection.

simp.text: The continents moved laterally rather than remaining fixed
He used evidence from a large number of sciences
His idea is at the heart of plate tectonics.
Plate tectonics is in many respects quite different
Yet it is a descendant

paras.main: Wegener dùng nhiều ngành khoa học; kiến tạo mảng là hậu duệ nhưng khác nhiều mặt.

sents: When I started writing about Wegener's life and work, one of the most intriguing things about him for me was that, although he came up with a theory on continental drift, he was not a geologist.
He trained as an astronomer and pursued a career in atmospheric physics.
When he proposed the theory of continental displacements in 1912, he was a lecturer in physics and astronomy at the University of Marburg, in southern Germany.
However, he was not an 'unknown'.
In 1906 he had set a world record (with his brother Kurt) for time aloft in a hot-air balloon: 52 hours.
Between 1906 and 1908 he had taken part in a highly publicized and extremely dangerous expedition to the coast of northeast Greenland.

He had also made a name for himself amongst a small circle of meteorologists and atmospheric physicists in Germany as the author of a textbook, Thermodynamics of the Atmosphere (1911), and of a number of interesting scientific papers.

simp.text: For me, one of the most intriguing things was that he was not a geologist
He trained as an astronomer and worked in atmospheric physics
In 1912 he was a lecturer.
However, he was not an 'unknown'
In 1906 he set a world record
He took part in an extremely dangerous expedition
He made a name among a small circle

paras.main: Wegener không phải nhà địa chất, nhưng đã có tiếng.

sents: As important as Wegener's work on continental drift has turned out to be, it was largely a sideline to his interest in atmospheric physics, geophysics, and paleoclimatology, and thus I have been at great pains to put Wegener's work on continental drift in the larger context of his other scientific work, and in the even larger context of atmospheric sciences in his lifetime.
This is a 'continental drift book' only to the extent that Wegener was interested in that topic and later became famous for it.

My treatment of his other scientific work is no less detailed, though I certainly have devoted more attention to the reception of his ideas on continental displacement, as they were much more controversial than his other work.

simp.text: Continental drift was largely a sideline; I put it in a larger context.
This is a 'continental drift book' only to the extent he was interested in it.
My treatment of other work is no less detailed, though more attention goes to the reception.

paras.main: Tác giả đặt trôi dạt lục địa trong bối cảnh công việc khoa học rộng hơn.

sents: Readers interested in the specific detail of Wegener's career will see that he often stopped pursuing a given line of investigation (sometimes for years on end), only to pick it up later.
I have tried to provide guideposts to his rapidly shifting interests by characterizing different phases of his life as careers in different sciences, which is reflected in the titles of the chapters.
Thus, the index should be a sufficient guide for those interested in a particular aspect of Wegener's life but perhaps not all of it.
My own feeling, however, is that the parts do not make as much sense on their own as do all of his activities taken together.
In this respect I urge readers to try to experience Wegener's life as he lived it, with all the interruptions, changes of mind, and renewed efforts this entailed.

simp.text: He often stopped a line of investigation and picked it up later.
I provided guideposts through chapter titles.
The index is a guide for a particular aspect.
However, the parts do not make as much sense on their own
I urge readers to experience his life as he lived it.

paras.main: Tác giả khuyên đọc toàn bộ để hiểu cả cuộc đời Wegener.

sents: Wegener left behind a few published works but, as was standard practice, these reported the results of his work - not the journey he took to reach that point.
Only a few hundred of the many thousands of letters he wrote and received in his lifetime have survived and he didn't keep notebooks or diaries that recorded his life and activities.

He was not active (with a few exceptions) in scientific societies, and did not seek to find influence or advance his ideas through professional contacts and politics, spending most of his time at home in his study reading and writing, or in the field collecting observations.

simp.text: His published works reported results, not the journey.
Few letters survived; no notebooks or diaries.
He was not active in societies and did not seek influence

paras.main: Wegener để lại ít tài liệu và không tìm kiếm ảnh hưởng.

sents: Some famous scientists, such as Newton, Darwin, and Einstein, left mountains of written material behind, hundreds of notebooks and letters numbering in the tens of thousands.
Others, like Michael Faraday, left extensive journals of their thoughts and speculations, parallel to their scientific notebooks.
The more such material a scientist leaves behind, the better chance a biographer has of forming an accurate picture of how a scientist's ideas took shape and evolved.

simp.text: Newton, Darwin, Einstein left mountains of material.
Faraday left extensive journals.
The more material, the better chance a biographer has of an accurate picture

paras.main: Càng nhiều tài liệu thì người viết tiểu sử càng dễ.

sents: I am firmly of the opinion that most of us, Wegener included, are not in any real sense the authors of our own lives.

We plan, think, and act, often with apparent freedom, but most of the time our lives 'happen to us', and we only retrospectively turn this happenstance into a coherent narrative of fulfilled intentions.
This book, therefore, is a story both of the life and scientific work that Alfred Wegener planned and intended and of the life and scientific work that actually 'happened to him'.
These are, as I think you will soon see, not always the same thing.

simp.text: Most of us are not the authors of our own lives
We plan, but our lives 'happen to us'.
This book tells both the planned life and what happened.
They are not always the same.

paras.main: Con người ít kiểm soát cuộc đời; sách kể cả điều dự định và điều xảy ra.

groups.instr: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in Reading Passage 3?

items.q: Wegener's ideas about continental drift were widely disputed while he was alive.
items.exp: Đoạn 1 ③: cuốn sách là trọng tâm của `an international controversy in his lifetime`. `widely disputed while he was alive`.

items.q: The idea that the continents remained fixed in place was defended in a number of respected scientific publications.
items.exp: Không nói ý tưởng "lục địa cố định" được bảo vệ trong các ấn phẩm khoa học uy tín nào. Đoạn 2 chỉ nói Wegener đề xuất lục địa di chuyển ngang.

items.q: Wegener relied on a limited range of scientific fields to support his theory of continental drift.
items.exp: Đoạn 2 ②: `evidence from a large number of sciences`. Đề nói `limited range` → mâu thuẫn.

items.q: The similarities between Wegener's theory of continental drift and modern-day plate tectonics are enormous.
items.exp: Đoạn 2 ④: `Plate tectonics is in many respects quite different from Wegener's proposal`. Đề nói similarities are enormous → mâu thuẫn. ⚠️ Đoạn 2 ⑤ (`descendant`) là bẫy.

groups.instr: Complete the summary using the list of phrases, A-J, below.

items.q: One of the remarkable things about Wegener from a ______ is that although he proposed a theory of continental drift, he was not a geologist.
items.exp: **I** biographer's perspective · Đoạn 3 ①: `one of the most intriguing things about him for me` – tác giả viết tiểu sử nên là góc nhìn người viết tiểu sử. Cụm `from a ___` cần danh từ + perspective.

items.q: His ______ were limited to atmospheric physics.
items.exp: **F** professional interests · Đoạn 3 ②: trained as astronomer, career in atmospheric physics. `His ___ were limited to` – số nhiều. ⚠️ J `narrow investigation` là số ít, không hợp `were`.

items.q: However, at the time he proposed his theory of continental drift in 1912, he was already a person of ______ .
items.exp: **A** modest fame · Đoạn 3 ④⑦: `not an 'unknown'`; `a name amongst a small circle`. `a person of ___` = `modest fame`.

items.q: Six years previously, there had been his ______ of 52 hours in a hot-air balloon, followed by his well-publicised but … of Greenland's coast.
items.exp: **C** record-breaking achievement · Đoạn 3 ⑤: `set a world record ... 52 hours`. `Six years previously` = 1906.

items.q: Six years previously, there had been his … of 52 hours in a hot-air balloon, followed by his well-publicised but ______ of Greenland's coast.
items.exp: **H** hazardous exploration · Đoạn 3 ⑥: `highly publicized and extremely dangerous expedition`. `well-publicised but ___` = `hazardous exploration`.

items.q: With the publication of his textbook on thermodynamics, he had also come to the attention of a ______ of German scientists.
items.exp: **E** select group · Đoạn 3 ⑦: `a small circle of meteorologists and atmospheric physicists` → `select group`.

groups.instr: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

items.q: What is Mott T Greene doing in the fifth paragraph?
items.exp: Đoạn 5 ④⑤: các phần không có nhiều ý nghĩa nếu đứng riêng; tác giả khuyến khích đọc để trải nghiệm trọn vẹn cuộc đời Wegener. `explaining why it is desirable to read the whole book`. A, C, D không khớp.

options.t: describing what motivated him to write the book
explaining why it is desirable to read the whole book
suggesting why Wegener pursued so many different careers
indicating what aspects of Wegener's life interested him most

items.q: What is said about Wegener in the sixth paragraph?
items.exp: Đoạn 6 ③: không hoạt động trong hội khoa học, không tìm cách tạo ảnh hưởng qua quan hệ và chính trị. `not a particularly ambitious person`. B sai (không giữ nhật ký); C, D không có.

options.t: He was not a particularly ambitious person.
He kept a record of all his scientific observations.
He did not adopt many of the scientific practices of the time.
He enjoyed discussing new discoveries with other scientists.

items.q: What does Greene say about some other famous scientists?
items.exp: Đoạn 7 ③: tài liệu càng nhiều thì người viết tiểu sử càng dễ hình dung chính xác. Newton, Darwin, Einstein để lại nhiều → `easier subjects to write about than Wegener` (Wegener để lại ít).

options.t: Their published works had a greater impact than Wegener's did.
They had fewer doubts about their scientific ideas than Wegener did.
Their scientific ideas were more controversial than Wegener's.
They are easier subjects to write about than Wegener.

items.q: What is Greene's main point in the final paragraph?
items.exp: Đoạn 8 ①②: `most of us ... are not in any real sense the authors of our own lives`; cuộc đời `happen to us`. `People have little control over many aspects of their lives`.

options.t: It is not enough in life to have good intentions.
People need to plan carefully if they want to succeed.
People have little control over many aspects of their lives.

exercises.q:
**A. Simplify** – tìm [S]–[V]:
1. `To convince investors and developers that installing green roofs is worthwhile, economic arguments are still the most important.`
2. `The statistician Andrew Gelman claims that 'their research designs have enough degrees of freedom that they could take their data to support just about any theory at all'.`
3. `He trained as an astronomer and pursued a career in atmospheric physics.`

**B. Đại từ:** `this group` (P2 đoạn 3⑥) chỉ ai? · `These countries` (P1 đoạn C④) chỉ ai? · `They` (P2 đoạn 7④) chỉ ai?

**C. Paraphrase:** `impediment` – ? · `supplanted` – ? · `intriguing` – ? · `retrospectively` – ?

**D.** Vì sao P3 Q30 là **NO** chứ không phải YES dù câu ⑤ nói `descendant`?

---
exercises.a:
**A.**
1. [S] economic arguments [V] are (the most important); `To convince ...` là mục đích, bỏ đi.
2. [S] The statistician Andrew Gelman [V] claims (that ...); mệnh đề trong dấu nháy là nội dung được tường thuật.
3. [S] He [V] trained / pursued.

**B.** `this group` = nhóm được khen về trí thông minh; `These countries` = Hoa Kỳ và Canada (North America); `They` = Yeager và Walton.

**C.** `impediment` – `obstacle`; `supplanted` – `replaced`; `intriguing` – `fascinating`; `retrospectively` – `looking back`.

**D.** Câu ④ nói kiến tạo mảng `in many respects quite different` so với đề xuất của Wegener. Câu ⑤ chỉ nói quan hệ nối dõi (`descendant`), không nói giống nhau nhiều. Câu hỏi nói "similarities ... are enormous" nên mâu thuẫn → NO.
